description.value: Task-fMRI comparison of reward anticipation in cigarette smokers and nonsmokers, testing whether striatal responses to immediate versus equally preferred delayed rewards differ between groups.

Cross-sectional observational comparison of smokers and nonsmokers. Both groups performed the same immediate/delayed reward task. Smokers were not required to abstain and were invited to smoke before scanning. A subset completed a post-task delay-discounting reassessment.

definition.value: Signal during anticipation of immediate vs. delayed rewards (which were equally preferred) was compared in whole-brain analysis.

value: Signal was significantly greater during the anticipation of immediate reward in regions including bilateral caudate/putamen/ventral striatum, bilateral insula, bilateral prefrontal cortex/frontal pole, bilateral superior frontal gyrus, bilateral thalamus, brain stem, and anterior cingulate cortex/supplementary motor cortex.

definition.value: We compared this “immediate > delayed” effect between smokers and nonsmokers.

value: We observed a larger “immediate > delayed” effect among smokers than nonsmokers in several regions, including the right ventral striatum, bilateral caudate, right putamen, left thalamus, left hippocampus/parahippocampal gyrus and lateral occipital cortex.

Validation of dsGrid, a dual-site TMS grid-search targeting method, by comparing individualized parietal targets with conventional P3 targets using resting-state connectivity, task-based connectivity, and task-evoked BOLD activity in 47 healthy adults.

One healthy cohort completed an MRI session and a separate TMS session. The MRI session included structural imaging, two resting-state runs, and five force-tracking runs. The TMS session established individualized dsGrid targets. Imaging comparisons were within participants between dsGrid and P3 locations, not between stimulation arms.
Participants enrolled in a clinical trial completed MRI and TMS sessions for validation of dsGrid targeting.

recruitment_method.value: Participants enrolled in a clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05103176).

value: We hypothesized that dsGrid targeting would more accurately capture individual differences in parietal-motor connectivity and task-related neural activity compared to the group-based P3 target.
